command: node --test (166 tests); DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1 web profile with the stand-in model: a bound conversation in a real open-source project, one read call making a turn meaningful (DSH_AWR_CHECKPOINT_MIN_TOOLS=1), the checkpoint read back from AWR (docs/evidence/DSH-030)

checks.name: After meaningful turns the model is prompted to checkpoint, and the digest, next action and open loops are written by the model, not generated by the plugin
checks.details: An agent/turn-stopping listener steers the conversation once, after a turn that wrote, edited or ran something or made at least three tool calls other than awr's, with a request to compile the context and save a checkpoint with the awr tool and to write the digest, next action and open loops itself. It does not ask when the model already checkpointed in the turn or within five minutes (a failed checkpoint does not count), when the turn was already asked, or when the conversation is unbound; errors in it never reach DSH. In DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1 (web profile) a bound conversation's turn ran five steps (read, the request, context compile, session checkpoint, a reply): the plugin decided asked, the next stop of the turn already_asked, and AWR held a checkpoint whose digest, next action and open loop were the text the model wrote in its own awr tool call (docs/evidence/DSH-030/live-dsh.json). The plugin runs no awr at a turn boundary (tested: it has no way to) and the request holds only placeholders. Ten mutation checks fail tests. A finding fixed on the way: the awr tool had turned ContextIncomplete into an error without the context hash, so the model could not checkpoint an incomplete context. Limits: the model was a stand-in that does what it is scripted to; the thresholds (three tool calls, five minutes) are guesses and settings; the web profile, not the desktop shell.
criteria: After meaningful turns the model is prompted to checkpoint and the saved digest, next action and open loops are written by the model from the conversation, not generated by the plugin.

checks.name: A session disposal never ends the AWR session as completed
checks.details: The agent/disposed listeners only drop what the plugin remembers about a conversation; a test shows no awr call is made at disposal and, by reading the library, that no file but commands.js builds a session end (the user's /awr end) and none builds a work complete (a work complete runs only when the model asks for it through the awr tool). An ended AWR session cannot be bound again under the same id (docs/binding.md), so the session is left active and the next conversation continues it or starts a successor. Limit: DSH's own disposal was not triggered in the live run; the guarantee is that the plugin does nothing on it.
criteria: A session disposal never ends the AWR session as completed.
